original_record.question:
Marta sticks several triangles on top of each other and makes a star that way. What is the minimum number of triangles she has used?
<image1>
original_record.subject: combinatorial geometry

inventory.image1: single filled irregular five-point star, left/right tips on one horizontal support line, top point left of center, bottom-left arm longest; no labels or internal lines
inventory.native_construction: five frozen outer tips; all concave vertices are exact intersections of pentagram diagonals, not a regular-star substitution

answer_verification.method: Lower bound: any triangle contained in this star cannot contain two adjacent outer tips, because their connecting segment crosses the exterior notch. Any three of five cyclic outer tips include an adjacent pair, so one triangle covers at most two tips; five tips require at least3 triangles. Upper bound: exact rational clipping verifies each of three frozen triangles lies in the star, and inclusion-exclusion gives union area exactly equal to star area.
